title: map_board_load error returns leak the partially-built board
evidence: append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = strings_clone(name, allocator), kind = kind, pos = {f32(px), f32(py)}}) ... return {}, "map_board_load: malformed spawn candidate" (same pattern at map.odin:296,300,305,327,335,380,388,410,413,416,419,422). Empirically verified: `odin test` on a load failing at 'malformed spawn candidate' reports `+++ leak 256B @ 0xCD4800038 [map.odin:319:map_board_load()]`.
detail: `return {}` overwrites the named return `b`, orphaning every allocation made before the error (district name clones, attribution, candidates, render_dots, district_start, partial polys). The app's fallback path keeps running with leaked memory; dev leak-CI would flag it.
recommended_fix: On every error return, destroy the partial board first (e.g. set err, defer-run map_board_destroy(&b) when err != "") before zeroing the named return.

title: test_board_destroy deletes string literals — invalid free that aborts under the default allocator
detail: delete() on static string data frees read-only memory. Odin's test tracking allocator only warns, but under a plain default allocator the process aborts (verified SIGABRT). Latent crash on every run of the two new growth tests.
recommended_fix: In test_board, build names with make/cloned bytes (or a shared heap string) so test_board_destroy's delete is legal — or drop the delete loop for literals.

title: Slices/strings allocated with the `allocator` param are freed via context.allocator — bad frees
detail: Plain slices and strings don't carry their allocator; delete() frees via context.allocator. Any caller passing a non-default allocator (both shipped tests pass temp_allocator) gets bad frees; app/harness only survive because their param happens to equal context.allocator.
recommended_fix: Free slices/strings explicitly with the `allocator` param (mem.free(raw_data(x), len, allocator)), or store dynamic arrays which carry their allocator.

title: dublin-shot exits 0 (success) when PNG export fails
detail: ExportImage failure is printed but never propagated: run_dublin_shot unconditionally returns 0 and prints success, so a scripted KYLE gate passes with missing captures.
recommended_fix: Have dublin_shot_capture return bool, OR the failures in run_dublin_shot, and return non-zero when any capture fails to write.

title: Docs claim district-scoped ATTACH draws; the implemented ring is global and the invariant is unpinned
evidence: core/map.odin header: "the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's OWN district's pool (an estate never crosses a district boundary), and the derived cluster view is unchanged (radius adjacency) — the district scoping at the DRAW makes cross-district estates unreachable by construction." Against growth.odin:537-546: "The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped)" with `for k in 0..<len(board.candidates) { ... append(ring, u32(k)) }` (no district filter). demos/dublin_board.dem: "the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's district pool — a cluster never crosses a district boundary". map_test.odin:13 claims "family stays WITHIN the anchor's district" but no test asserts it.
detail: Three shipped documents state an invariant no code enforces: district_start/candidate_district are read by no growth code (grep-verified), and cross-district estates are reachable by construction. Stage-2 work reading map.odin/demos inherits a false contract.
recommended_fix: Align the map.odin header, demo header, and test comment with the ruled global-ring interplay — or actually scope the ring via district_start and pin it with a test.

title: Board and Dublin render cache have no teardown despite comments claiming one exists
evidence: map_board_destroy doc: "call once when the process is done with it — the app frees at exit, the harness's board cache lives for the process". dublin.odin:87: "// dublin_render_destroy — free the cache's buffers (called by view teardown)." Grep: map_board_destroy is called only from core/map_test.odin; dublin_render_destroy only from dublin_render_ensure (dublin.odin:104). app/main.odin defers catalogs_destroy/audio_destroy (lines 276/329) but never map_board_destroy(&app.board).
detail: The app never frees the board (plus its ~811KB terrain_cells cache) at exit; the only callers are the tests. The code's own contract comments assert teardown wiring that does not exist; dev tracking-allocator runs flag it.
recommended_fix: Call map_board_destroy(&app.board) and dublin_render_destroy at app exit alongside the existing catalogs/audio teardown defers — or correct the comments.

title: Growth ring scratch allocates via implicit context.allocator in core; the `alloc` parameter is dead
evidence:
growth_board_ring_scan :: proc(board: ^Map_Board, t: ^Topology, anchor: [2]i32, sep, radius: i32, ring: ^[dynamic]u32, alloc := context.temp_allocator) -> i32 { ... if d2 >= lo2 && d2 <= hi2 {
			append(ring, u32(k)) — `alloc` is never referenced. Plus: "// v2-dublin-board: the attach ring scratch (temp-allocated per window —" above `ring_scratch: [dynamic]u32` (a nil array whose appends fall back to context.allocator), and `ring: [dynamic]u32` in growth_board_cluster_has_room (line 559).
detail: The comment claims temp-allocation but no explicit allocator is wired (ODN-18: core never makes without an explicit allocator argument); allocations ride whatever context.allocator the step caller holds, and the declared `alloc` param is unused.
recommended_fix: Create the scratch/ring arrays with make(..., context.temp_allocator) so appends use the intended arena, and remove or actually use the dead alloc parameter.
